projects.title: Toilet Replacement
projects.blurb: Swap an old toilet for a new one — remove, set a fresh wax ring, and seal it leak-free.
top_questions: What if my shutoff valve leaks when I turn it back on?
Do I need to replace the flange or can I reuse it?
What size supply line do I need?
How do I stop the new toilet from rocking?
common_mistakes: Over-tightening the tank bolts and cracking the porcelain
Reusing an old, compressed wax ring
Forgetting to replace corroded closet bolts
Not shimming an uneven floor, causing the toilet to rock
helpful_tips: Spray penetrating oil on the old bolts the night before.
Buy two wax rings just in case the first one shifts.
Take a photo of the supply line before disconnecting.
Replace the shutoff valve while the water is already off.

experiences.author: Mike R.
experiences.title: Champion 4 install — 90 minutes start to finish
experiences.body: Did this in my guest bath. The included wax ring was fine but I always double up. Floor was slightly uneven so I added two plastic shims and caulked the base. Zero rocking, zero leaks.

experiences.author: Sarah L.
experiences.title: First time and it actually went great
experiences.body: Was terrified of this but the old bolts came off with penetrating oil. Hardest part was lifting the old toilet — get a friend. New supply line was needed, the old one was too short.

experiences.author: Dwayne P.
experiences.title: Flange was cracked — glad I checked
experiences.body: Pulled the old one and the flange was broken. Added a repair ring before the wax. Adds 30 min but saves you a callback. Always inspect the flange before you set the bowl.

threads.author: NewHomeowner22
threads.question: My shutoff valve is the old multi-turn type and drips a little. Should I replace it during the swap?

replies.author: Mike R.
replies.body: 100% yes. Water's already off — swap it for a quarter-turn valve. $12 part and you'll never fight it again.

replies.author: Sarah L.
replies.body: I did exactly this. Took 10 extra minutes and the drip is gone.

projects.title: Water Heater Replacement
projects.blurb: Replace a failing tank water heater — drain, disconnect, set the new unit, and relight.
top_questions: Do I need a permit to replace my own water heater?
Gas or electric — what's harder?
Should I add an expansion tank?
How do I safely drain the old tank?
common_mistakes: Not turning off the gas/breaker before draining
Forgetting an expansion tank where code requires it
Cross-threading the flex connectors
Skipping the drip pan on a second floor
helpful_tips: Connect a hose and drain into a floor drain or outside.
Use flexible water and gas connectors — far easier than rigid.
Add an expansion tank; many codes now require it.
Test for gas leaks with soapy water on every joint.

experiences.author: Carlos M.
experiences.title: Rheem 50gal gas swap — get a helper
experiences.body: These tanks are heavy full and awkward empty. Drained overnight to be safe. Flex connectors made the reconnect painless. Soapy-water tested every gas joint, lit fine on the first try.

experiences.author: Janet K.
experiences.title: Electric unit — easier than I feared
experiences.body: Killed the breaker, confirmed with a tester. The only surprise was needing an expansion tank for our city code. Added one and passed inspection.

threads.author: FixItFred
threads.question: Is it worth going tankless instead while I'm at it?

replies.author: Carlos M.
replies.body: Only if your gas line and venting can handle it — otherwise it's a much bigger job. For a straight swap, a tank is a 4-hour afternoon.

projects.title: Kitchen Faucet Installation
projects.blurb: Replace a kitchen or bath faucet — disconnect supply lines, mount, and connect the new one.
top_questions: Why won't the old mounting nut come loose?
Do I need a basin wrench?
Do new faucets come with supply lines?
How tight should the connections be?
common_mistakes: Skipping the basin wrench and rounding the nuts
Over-tightening plastic supply nuts
Forgetting plumber's tape on threaded joints
Not clearing the old gunk/caulk from the sink deck
helpful_tips: A basin wrench is a $15 lifesaver for tight spaces.
Hand-tighten plus a quarter turn on supply lines — no more.
Run a bead of silicone under the base plate.
Keep a bucket and towel under the cabinet.

experiences.author: Tina W.
experiences.title: Pull-down sprayer upgrade
experiences.body: Old nuts were seized — the basin wrench saved me. New faucet came with supply lines so I didn't need to buy any. 50 minutes including cleanup.

experiences.author: Omar S.
experiences.title: Easiest plumbing win ever
experiences.body: Honestly my favorite beginner project. Took photos before disconnecting and just reversed the steps. The hardest part was lying under the sink.

threads.author: KitchenReno
threads.question: My new faucet has 3 holes but my sink has 4. What do I do with the extra?

replies.author: Tina W.
replies.body: Add a soap dispenser or a deck plate that covers all four. Most faucets include an optional plate.

projects.title: Garbage Disposal Replacement
projects.blurb: Swap a dead disposal — disconnect, twist off the old unit, and mount the new one.
top_questions: Can I reuse the old mounting ring?
How do I wire it without an electrician?
Why is my new disposal leaking at the dishwasher hose?
Do I need to remove the knockout plug?
common_mistakes: Forgetting to punch out the dishwasher knockout plug
Not supporting the heavy unit while twisting it on
Reusing a worn mounting gasket
Loose discharge tube clamp causing leaks
helpful_tips: If the brand matches, the old mount often reuses — huge time saver.
Punch the knockout plug BEFORE installing if you have a dishwasher.
Rest the unit on a paint can while you line up the mount.
Reset button on the bottom fixes most 'dead' disposals first.

experiences.author: Greg H.
experiences.title: Same brand = 25 minute swap
experiences.body: Went Badger to Badger so the mounting ring stayed. Just unplugged, twisted off, twisted on, reconnected. Knocked out the dishwasher plug first — learned that one the hard way years ago.

threads.author: QuietPlease
threads.question: Any recommendations for a quieter unit? Mine sounds like a jet engine.

replies.author: Greg H.
replies.body: Step up to a 3/4 or 1 HP insulated model. The sound insulation is night and day.

projects.title: Drywall Hole Repair
projects.blurb: Patch holes from dings to doorknob-sized — mesh, mud, sand, and paint to invisible.
top_questions: Mesh tape or paper tape for the patch?
How many coats of mud do I really need?
How do I match the existing wall texture?
Why does my patch show through after painting?
common_mistakes: Applying mud too thick and over-sanding
Skipping primer so the patch flashes through paint
Not feathering the edges wide enough
Rushing coats before they fully dry
helpful_tips: Three thin coats beat one thick coat every time.
Feather each coat wider than the last.
Prime the patch before painting or it'll show.
Match texture with a spray can of wall texture.

experiences.author: Lena F.
experiences.title: Doorknob hole — California patch method
experiences.body: Cut a square, used the California/butterfly patch so no framing needed. Three coats of lightweight mud, sanded between, primed, painted. You truly cannot find it.

experiences.author: Marcus T.
experiences.title: Texture match was the tricky part
experiences.body: The patch itself was easy. Matching the orange-peel texture took a couple practice sprays on cardboard first. Glad I tested before hitting the wall.

threads.author: RenterRick
threads.question: Getting my deposit back — what's the fastest way to fix a dozen nail holes?

replies.author: Lena F.
replies.body: Lightweight spackle with your finger, let dry, light sand, dab of matching paint. 20 minutes for all of them.

projects.title: Ceiling Fan Installation
projects.blurb: Replace a light or install a new ceiling fan — brace box, wire, and balance the blades.
top_questions: Do I need a fan-rated electrical box?
Which wire is which on an old fixture?
Why does my fan wobble?
Can I put a fan where a light used to be?
common_mistakes: Hanging a fan from a standard light box (not rated for weight)
Skipping the downrod for low ceilings — or needing one for high
Not using the balancing kit for wobble
Loose wire nuts in the canopy
helpful_tips: Always swap to a fan-rated brace box — it carries the motion load.
Take a phone photo of the existing wiring first.
Assemble the fan on the ground as much as possible.
Use the included balancing clips to kill the wobble.

experiences.author: Priya N.
experiences.title: Light-to-fan conversion done right
experiences.body: The old box was not fan-rated, so I installed a saddle brace box from the attic. That's the step people skip and regret. Wiring was straightforward, blades balanced with the kit.

threads.author: WobblyWanda
threads.question: Installed fine but it wobbles on high. Help?

replies.author: Priya N.
replies.body: Check that all blade screws are tight first, then use the stick-on balancing weights. Move one weight along a blade until the wobble drops.

projects.title: Light Fixture Replacement
projects.blurb: Swap a dated fixture for something fresh — kill power, match wires, mount, done.
top_questions: How do I know the power is really off?
What if there's no ground wire in an old house?
Black to black, white to white — always?
My new fixture is heavier — is the box okay?
common_mistakes: Relying on the switch instead of the breaker
Not testing wires with a voltage tester
Ignoring a missing ground in older homes
Pinching wires when pushing the fixture up
helpful_tips: Kill the breaker AND test every wire before touching.
No ground? Connect to the box if it's metal and grounded.
Hold the fixture with a hook or helper while wiring.
Tuck wires neatly so the canopy sits flush.

experiences.author: Brett A.
experiences.title: Dining room pendant in 30 min
experiences.body: Genuinely the easiest electrical project. Breaker off, tested, matched the wires, mounted. The only tip: support the new fixture so you're not wiring one-handed.

threads.author: OldHouseOwner
threads.question: 1950s house, the box only has black and white — no ground. Safe to install?

replies.author: Brett A.
replies.body: If the metal box is grounded you can pigtail the fixture ground to it. If unsure, a $10 outlet tester or an electrician's quick look is worth it.

projects.title: Smart Doorbell Install
projects.blurb: Install a video doorbell — wire to existing chime or go battery, then set up the app.
top_questions: Will it work with my existing doorbell wiring?
Do I need the chime adapter (jumper)?
My transformer is 16V — is that enough?
How do I mount on brick or stucco?
common_mistakes: Forgetting the chime adapter, causing a buzzing chime
Undersized transformer — low voltage warnings
Drilling brick without a masonry bit
Not turning off the breaker for the doorbell circuit
helpful_tips: Check your transformer voltage first — most need 16–24V AC.
Install the chime adapter if you keep your mechanical chime.
Use the included angle wedge to aim at the walkway.
A masonry bit + anchors are a must for brick.

experiences.author: Hannah B.
experiences.title: Ring Pro on brick — wedge mount helped
experiences.body: Transformer was already 16V so wired install worked. The chime adapter stopped the buzzing. Masonry bit through the brick was the only 'real tool' moment. App setup was 5 minutes.

threads.author: RentSmart
threads.question: No existing doorbell wiring — is battery version reliable?

replies.author: Hannah B.
replies.body: Battery versions are great now. You'll recharge every 1–3 months depending on traffic. Totally fine for an apartment.

projects.title: Deck Staining
projects.blurb: Clean, prep, and stain a wood deck to protect it and bring back the color.
top_questions: Do I need to strip the old stain first?
How long should the deck dry after cleaning?
Solid, semi-transparent, or transparent stain?
What's the best temperature/weather to stain?
common_mistakes: Staining damp wood — it won't absorb and peels
Skipping the cleaning/brightening step
Applying in direct hot sun (dries too fast, lap marks)
Too-thick coats that stay tacky
helpful_tips: Let the deck dry 24–48 hours after washing.
Stain in the shade or on an overcast day.
Work in 2–3 board sections to avoid lap marks.
A pump sprayer + back-brushing gives the best finish.

experiences.author: Tom V.
experiences.title: Semi-transparent over a weekend
experiences.body: Pressure washed Saturday, let it dry all day Sunday, stained Monday evening when the sun was off it. Sprayer plus back-brush was way faster than a roller and looked even.

threads.author: GreyDeck
threads.question: My deck is grey and weathered. Can I stain right over it?

replies.author: Tom V.
replies.body: Use a deck cleaner/brightener first — it pulls out the grey and opens the wood so the stain actually soaks in.

projects.title: Interior Room Painting
projects.blurb: Repaint a room like a pro — prep, cut in, roll, and get crisp edges.
top_questions: Do I really need to prime?
How do I get sharp lines without bleed?
One coat or two?
What roller nap for my wall texture?
common_mistakes: Skipping prep — dust and grease ruin adhesion
Pulling tape after the paint fully dries (peels the edge)
Overloading the roller and leaving drips
Cheap brushes that shed bristles
helpful_tips: Prep is 80% of a good paint job — wash, patch, sand.
Pull tape while the paint is still slightly wet for crisp lines.
Two thin coats almost always beat one thick coat.
Buy one good 2.5" angled brush — it lasts years.

experiences.author: Aisha R.
experiences.title: Bold accent wall — tape trick works
experiences.body: Caulked the tape edge with a thin paint line first, let it seal, then painted the color. Pulled tape while wet. Razor-sharp line, zero bleed. Game changer.

threads.author: FirstApartment
threads.question: Going from dark green to white. How many coats?

replies.author: Aisha R.
replies.body: Prime with a tinted gray primer, then 2 coats of white. Trying to do it without primer over dark = endless coats.

projects.title: HVAC Filter Replacement
projects.blurb: Keep your system healthy — find the right size, orientation, and swap schedule.
top_questions: Which way does the arrow point?
What MERV rating should I use?
How often should I really change it?
Why are there filters in two places?
common_mistakes: Installing the filter backwards (arrow should point toward the unit)
Going too high on MERV and choking airflow
Forgetting a return-grille filter elsewhere in the house
Buying the wrong size — measure, don't guess
helpful_tips: Arrow points in the direction of airflow — toward the furnace/blower.
MERV 8–11 is the sweet spot for most homes.
Write the date on the filter edge with a marker.
Set a 90-day phone reminder (30 with pets).

experiences.author: Dell C.
experiences.title: The 5-minute money saver
experiences.body: Cannot believe I paid someone for this. Slid the old one out, noted the arrow, slid the new one in same direction. Wrote the date on it. Airflow noticeably better.

threads.author: AllergyMom
threads.question: Can I use the highest MERV filter for allergies?

replies.author: Dell C.
replies.body: Careful — too-high MERV restricts airflow and strains the blower. MERV 11–13 is usually the max a residential system likes.

projects.title: Interior Door Replacement
projects.blurb: Hang a new slab or pre-hung door — measure, set hinges, and get it swinging true.
top_questions: Slab door or pre-hung — which is easier?
How do I transfer the hinge locations?
Why does my door swing open or shut on its own?
How much gap should I leave around the door?
common_mistakes: Buying a slab and fighting hinge/latch alignment
Not shimming a pre-hung frame plumb
Mortising hinges too deep or too shallow
Forgetting the swing direction when ordering
helpful_tips: A pre-hung door is far more forgiving for beginners.
Use the old door as a template for a slab.
A self-swinging door means the frame isn't plumb — shim it.
Nickel-thickness gap around the door is the standard.

experiences.author: Rosa D.
experiences.title: Used old slab as a template
experiences.body: Stacked the old and new doors, traced the hinges and latch, chiseled the mortises. Tedious but it lined up perfectly. A door swinging on its own = check plumb, which fixed mine.

threads.author: DraftyDoor
threads.question: New door has a big gap at the bottom. Normal?

replies.author: Rosa D.
replies.body: A bit of gap is normal for clearance over flooring, but if it's huge you can add a sweep or trim the jamb. What's your flooring height?
